findings.title: Existing realms never receive the new Groups scopes/resources
findings.body: Adding Groups to SCHEMA is not applied to realms that already have an admin-permissions client. init() returns immediately when realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() is non-null, so existing V2 realms keep only the old Users/Clients scopes and all-resource resources. Group scopes such as view-members and the all-groups resource will be missing; creating group permissions then fails in getOrCreateResource with 'No scopes found' (or getScope throws), and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission can evaluate a null all-groups resource. This needs an upgrade/migration path or an ensure-missing-scopes/resources update.

findings.title: Per-group resources are created without a resource type
findings.body: getOrCreateResource creates a resource for a group and updates its scopes, but never calls resource.setType(resourceType). GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission enumerates group grants with resourceStore.findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...), so per-group resources created here are invisible to that lookup (only the type-tagged 'Groups' all-resource is returned). As a result group-scoped member permissions cannot be found for user search/listing. Set the resource type when creating the resource.

findings.title: Group member permission lookup uses authz resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission the callback calls hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...), but hasPermission treats its first argument as a group id and looks it up with resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). For a per-group resource the resource name is the group id, not the resource id, so the lookup falls back to the all-groups resource (or fails), and the method adds groupResource.getId() (an authz resource id) to the granted set. UsersResource then puts those ids into UserModel.GROUPS, so per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants are ignored and an all-groups grant can make user search return no users. Use groupResource.getName() (the group id) or evaluate the resource directly, and add the group id, not the resource id.

findings.title: canManage() grants group management with only VIEW scope
findings.body: The global canManage() returns true when the caller has only VIEW on all groups because it evaluates hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE). GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup calls auth.groups().requireManage() before creating a top-level group, so a caller with view-only all-groups permission can create groups. canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires MANAGE; canManage() should require only MANAGE as well.

findings.title: Groups resource type is not resolved to a group name for display
findings.body: getResourceName handles only USERS. For a policy with resourceType Groups it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), and because group resources are named with the group id, the admin console/events show the raw id instead of the group name (and there is no 'All groups' label). Add a GROUPS branch analogous to the USERS branch.

findings.title: Group removal cleanup is not registered for V2
findings.body: Group-removal cleanup is still gated on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and not ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. In a V2-only deployment the listener is never registered, so deleting a group leaves its Groups resource and policies orphaned. If both features are enabled, management(...).groups() returns GroupPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException, causing group deletion to fail. The new Groups resource type needs a V2-safe cleanup path.
